title: Delegated Approval Within and Outside the Window (base)
scenario_text:
Farthom Industries requires CMO approval for any marketing purchase over $150,000. On October 30, the CMO Angela Reyes sent a written delegation email — copied to the General Counsel and archived in the Delegation of Authority (DoA) register — stating: 'For my parental leave from November 4 through November 28, I delegate marketing approval authority up to $250,000 to VP Marketing Priya Menon and to Marketing Director Alan Wu; either may approve within the amount limit. Purchases above $250,000 must wait for my return.'

On November 12, Alan Wu submits a purchase requisition to renew Farthom's marketing automation stack (Marketo, Drift, and 6sense) for one year. The line-item total is $220,000. The Coupa PR routing shows: Alan Wu → VP Marketing → CMO → CFO (exception threshold at $200,000). Alan's justification memo references the CMO's delegation and asks Procurement to release the PO after his own approval since VP Marketing Priya is traveling in a customer briefing this week.

The delegation email is visible in the DoA register with an active flag. Angela's auto-reply notes she returns November 29 and is not monitoring email during leave.
question: Given the delegation in place, whose approval is needed to release this $220,000 marketing-tools renewal purchase order?
choices: Marketing Director alone — she holds delegated authority for this purchase.
Marketing Director plus a courtesy notification to the CMO.
The full standard chain: Marketing Director, VP Marketing, CMO, then CFO for the exception threshold.
The CMO directly, since delegation of executive-level approvals is not permitted at Farthom.
